title: Latency-adaptive slice broker with KV reservation tokens
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a latency-adaptive slice broker that grants short-lived 'KV reservation tokens' to tenant slices in the continuous batching runtime. Tokens represent soft guarantees on KV residency and preemption immunity for a bounded window. The broker continuously adjusts token allocations based on observed tail-latency SLOs, recent KV hit-rate, and tenant weight. The goal is to reduce tail latency regressions caused by KV eviction churn while preserving fairness and overall GPU memory utilization.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New broker can allocate KV reservation tokens per-tenant and per-slice and enforce token lifetime without causing memory leaks.
2) Tail latency (p99) for latency-sensitive tenants decreases by >=15% on the test workload compared to baseline continuous-batcher without tokens.
3) Overall KV hit-rate change is <= 5% negative for best-effort tenants under mixed workloads (latency-sensitive + throughput-heavy).
4) No increase in OOM events on ci-gpu-cluster across 72h stress test. Memory telemetry shows expected KV slab compaction cycles.
5) Integration tests validate cooperative soft preemption and immediate hard preemption paths when tokens expire or are forcibly revoked.
technical_decisions: Use a two-tier token model: soft tokens (preemption delay + priority boost) and hard tokens (short non-preemptible window).
Token budget computed from per-GPU KV slab free space, tenant weight, and observed request arrival rate using EWMA for short-term smoothing.
Implement token accounting in the runtime lease manager; tokens are lightweight opaque IDs mapped to KV residency hints instead of immediate pinning of memory pages to avoid fragmentation.

Eviction policy: when under pressure, reclaim soft-token reservations by shrinking their effective reservation linearly before evicting; hard tokens are targeted last unless under emergency OOM conditions.
Preemption modes: cooperative yield (preferred), delayed interrupt (preemption with graceful KV snapshot), and immediate hard revoke (last resort).
design_tradeoffs: Pinned vs hinted reservation: true pinning reduces eviction jitter but increases fragmentation and hard-to-reclaim memory; we choose hinting plus polite eviction to balance latency vs utilization.
Token window length: longer windows reduce churn but can starve best-effort work; we picked a default 250ms soft window and 50ms hard window with autoscaling based on SLO pressure.

Centralized broker vs fully local per-GPU heuristic: centralized broker enables cross-GPU fairness and global budgeting but adds RPC coordination. We implement a hybrid: local broker uses global quotas refreshed every 500ms to avoid per-request RPCs.
implementation_notes: Runtime: add SliceBroker component into the batching coordinator responsible for token minting and lease transitions.
KV cache: extend metadata with reservation_token IDs and last_reserved_at timestamps; eviction scorer uses reserved weight.
Tracing: emit token_alloc, token_revoke, token_expire events with tenant_id, slice_id, token_type, and reason for downstream analysis.
Backwards compatibility: tokens are advisory; older workers without broker ignore reservation_token metadata (graceful rollout).
Rollout plan: feature-flagged in runtime-1.22 behind 'kv_token_broker' feature flag; default OFF for Dedicated until maturity.
experiment_results: Small-scale bench (4 tenants, 2 GPUs, mixed QPS): p99 for latency-sensitive tenants decreased from 220ms to 180ms (18%) with token broker enabled.
KV hit-rate: latency-sensitive tenant improved by 9%, best-effort tenant decreased by 3% under controlled mixing tests.
Memory churn: observed 30% fewer eviction cycles peaking under synthetic hotspot workload.
Regression: a tail case where aggressive token allocation caused starvation for an unweighted tenant; mitigated by adding a min-allocated-fraction per-GPU.
test_plan: Unit tests for token lifecycle and broker state machine.
Integration: end-to-end continuous batching with token broker enabled across 3-node GPU cluster; verify token invariants under noise and node failures.
Chaos: simulate worker restart during token grant and verify idempotent reclaim.
Perf: run existing slo-suite workload and compare p50/p95/p99 and KV hit-rate across baseline and token-broker.
Canary: release to small percentage of production traffic and monitor SLOs and memory signals for 48h before broader rollout.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike complete. Prototype token metadata stored alongside KV entries; validated eviction scorer honoring reserved weight (Avery).
2026-03-02: Implemented local broker and global quota refresher. Initial load tests show desired p99 improvements but discovered starvation scenario under uneven tenant weights (Sofia).

2026-03-08: Added min-allocated-fraction and linear decay for soft-token shrinking. Re-tested and starvation mitigated. Performance regression in best-effort p50 noted and accepted within 5% threshold.
2026-03-11: Design review with PM and SRE. PM requests dashboard surfaces: token allocation heatmap and token_revokes/sec. SRE requests additional alert for token_revokes > 100/min.
review_feedback: PM (Imran Patel): Add experiment that simulates sudden spike of small requests to ensure token churn doesn't amplify tail latency.
SRE (Lena Ortiz): Ensure token metadata TTL is strictly bounded to prevent stale reservations after node crash.
Design (Marco Silva): Consider UX for Console: surface per-tenant token burn-rate and allow operators to set emergency hard-revoke triggers.
Security (Priya Rao): Confirm that reservation metadata doesn't leak tenant identifiers in logs; mask tenant_id for console views.
open_questions: Should we expose a public SDK flag to request a 'reservation hint' for user-level clients (e.g., low-latency requests from critical paths)?
What global fairness policy should be default: strict proportional share by committed weight, or opportunistic smoothing favoring latency-sensitive tags?
How to tune the global refresher interval during high variance traffic to avoid oscillation?
comments: Sofia Martinez (2026-02-24): Initial prototype shows promise. Need to instrument memory fragmentation counters before wider tests.
Avery Chen (2026-03-03): Experiment added min-allocated-fraction=0.05 per GPU which prevented starvation in the 10T workload.
Imran Patel (2026-03-11): PM review: please add a short PRD blurb describing operator controls and expected defaults for Dedicated customers.
